title: Uniformizer reductions of diagonal coefficient diagrams
statement: Using the canonical finite class/trace comparison of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-finite-diagonal], using the finite realizations of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-finite-realization] and quotient-line comparisons of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-quotient-line], let a family be as in [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-category] and [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-diagrams], with Noetherian base $Y$. Its finite-reduction property means the following for every finite subextension $E$, every generator $\pi$ of the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_E$, and every $n\geq0$. There is a diagonal diagram over the actual quotient $A=\mathcal O_E/(\pi^{n+1})$ and a scalar compatibility from the integral family member along the quotient map. There is a positive power $N=\ell^{r+1}$ killing $A$ and invertible on the base and diagonal surface, and $A$ is finite. Give exact finite-coefficient realization equivalences with specified underlying-sheaf identifications. Their coefficient-unit isomorphisms are induced by unital ring-object identifications with the constant $A$ sheaf. Identify the quotient lines with the finite Cartier lines by requiring their composite from the integral root limit to be the actual projection to $\mu_N$, followed by $z\mapsto1\otimes z$ and the kernel-normalized root comparison. The supported-source identification is the direct image of the unit comparison. Under these identifications, the quotient diagonal arrow is precisely the canonical Cartier class of [def-sfb-geo-cartier-canonical-class]. The trace's ordinary realization/direct-image comparison is fixed on underlying sheaves and its derived comparison by the full universal unit. The quotient trace becomes exactly the trace of [sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology]: inverse to its positive unit/Chern splitting, followed by the constant summand projection. Both integration equalities are part of the quotient diagram. This quantifies over every positive uniformizer power, not only the ell-power cofinal levels.
